subject: MSA: Forum preference + injunctive carveouts (CrescentFin)
messages_1_subject: CrescentFin MSA - jurisdictional preferences and injunctive relief
messages_1_body:
Hi Lauren and team,

Thanks again for the call yesterday. Attached are our annotated MSA pages with a few asks we want to confirm before moving to signatures: primarily (1) narrow choice of forum to Massachusetts for any litigation, (2) carveouts for emergency injunctive relief to be permitted in any competent court pending arbitration, and (3) limited waiver language around equitable relief and provisional remedies.

We highlighted the proposed language on sections 14 (Dispute Resolution) and 15 (Injunctive Relief). Our GC wants explicit language that allows Crescent Financial to seek provisional relief in state or federal court in MA, but to return to arbitration for merits. Can you confirm whether Redwood will accept the jurisdiction lock to MA or if you will require a more flexible forum-selection clause?

Attaching: CrescentFin_MSA_Redlines_20270528.pdf

Katherine Hale
Director, Strategic Sourcing
Crescent Financial
messages_2_subject: Re: CrescentFin MSA - jurisdictional preferences and injunctive relief
messages_2_body:
Katherine — thanks, received and reviewed quickly. Looping in Markus (legal) and Laura (enterprise ops) to confirm Redwood's position. High level: we are comfortable with a carveout for provisional injunctive relief so long as the clause includes (a) a requirement to promptly move merits to arbitration, (b) a narrowly tailored scope for what qualifies as "emergency" relief, and (c) a mutual waiver of forum for disputes that are purely contractual and non-emergency.

We will need to push back on a strict Massachusetts-only forum for all litigation; our preference is (i) arbitration as the primary remedy, and (ii) either (A) a stated list of acceptable courts (MA or CA) for provisional relief, or (B) allowing emergency relief in any jurisdiction where the harm is occurring, with an agreement to arbitrate merits. Markus — can you propose language that preserves Crescent's ability to get immediate relief but avoids locking Redwood into one specific forum for every scenario?

Next steps: Markus to draft counter-language today; we will aim to consolidate and return to Crescent by EOD. Laura — can you confirm whether procurement needs the jurisdiction locked for ordering/system reasons?

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Sales Contracts (Americas)
Redwood Inference
messages_3_subject: Re: CrescentFin MSA - jurisdictional preferences and injunctive relief
messages_3_body:
Lauren — draft language below that I think balances both sides. I'm sending it back to Crescent as a clean section they can drop into the MSA.

--- DRAFT (proposed section for provisional remedies) ---
Notwithstanding the agreement to arbitrate disputes under Section 14, either party may seek provisional or injunctive relief in any state or federal court of competent jurisdiction to preserve the status quo or prevent irreparable harm. Such party shall promptly file for arbitration on the merits within 30 days following the grant of provisional relief, and the parties agree to stay any further litigation concerning the merits in favor of arbitration. The availability of provisional relief shall be narrowly construed and limited to circumstances where monetary damages are insufficient to remedy the harm.
--- end draft ---

On forum selection: we should decline a single-forum lock (MA-only). If Crescent insists we can agree to a limited provision naming two possible courts (Federal District of Massachusetts or U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California) for non-arbitral emergency relief, subject to the narrow proviso above.

I'll note: if Crescent absolutely requires MA-only, we will need an exec escalation and a legal risk acceptance from our side; that could trigger a small pricing concession per the deal team.

Markus Klein
Senior Counsel, Transactions
Redwood Inference
messages_4_subject: Re: CrescentFin MSA - jurisdictional preferences and injunctive relief (commercial implications)
messages_4_body:
Looping in commercial context: Crescent is a mid-market finance customer; deal value currently at $195k ARR with a one-year order form. If the legal team requires MA-only forum and this becomes a hard requirement, sales is ok to discuss a modest concession (1-2% credit on first year) but we should not set a precedent.

Also: procurement has asked whether signing in MA will affect our support and data residency commitments. Laura, please confirm operational impact — if none, that reduces our leverage. If there is an operational risk or additional cost tied to MA proceedings, share estimate here.

Action items: (1) Markus — finalize counter-language and flag any material legal exposures, (2) Laura — confirm ops impact, (3) Lauren — consolidate and send to Crescent by EOD.

Thanks — Priyom
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
messages_5_subject: Consolidated position: provisional relief carveout + arbitration procedure (CrescentFin MSA)
messages_5_body:
Katherine — thanks for the annotated copy and for the clear ask. We discussed internally and propose the following for Section 14/15: (a) Redwood accepts a narrowed provisional relief carveout allowing either party to seek emergency injunctive relief in any court of competent jurisdiction to preserve the status quo or prevent irreparable harm, (b) the party obtaining provisional relief must file for arbitration on the merits within 30 days and the parties will stay any further litigation on the merits, and (c) the language will explicitly state that provisional relief is to be narrowly construed and limited to situations where monetary damages are inadequate.

Regarding forum lock: Redwood cannot accept a Massachusetts-only forum for all disputes. If Crescent wants a preferred court list we can accept a two-court option (U.S. District Court for the District of Massachusetts OR U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California) for non-arbitral provisional relief. Otherwise we propose the "any court of competent jurisdiction" language coupled with the prompt-arbitration requirement.

We attached a clean annotated MSA segment (MSA_Annotated_v3.docx) with the exact text to drop in. Please let us know if Crescent can accept this compromise so we can move forward to signature and DocuSign. If your GC needs to escalate to leadership for the two-court option, flag that and we can pause for a quick phone call.

Attachments: MSA_Annotated_v3.docx

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Sales Contracts (Americas)
Redwood Inference
